chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: First professional recording with Hampton's small group
summary: At the Grand Terrace period he recorded with Hampton, Marshall Royal, Ray Perry, Vernon Alley, Irving Ashby and trumpeter Karl George, his first professional session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Sir Charles, when you were with Lionel and you were playing the Grand Terrace, you made a record session at that time, didn't you?

Yes, we made a very important record session there, to me, because it was my first professional recording, and it was done with Lionel, with a small group of musicians which included first Lee Young. I believe Lee Young was on some of the records on the drums. You can look this up but also Shadow Wilson came in the band later.
But the basic group was made up of Marshall Royal who played clarinet on the date, and Ray Perry

played violin, and some alto. But primarily Marshall played the clarinet and Ray Perry played the violin, and there was Vernon Alley, the bass player, he was on those records. He hadn't been replaced yet, and there was Lionel on the vibes, and Irving Ashby on guitar, and myself on piano.

And one of those dates was a trumpet player who later on left the group. Karl George. He was a very, very fine first trumpet player with a beautiful tone, who had played with Teddy Wilson's very fine, big band. And he had a beautiful sound. He was instrumental --

First trumpet. He was very instrumental in making that band sound beautiful, and together, because he was an excellent first trumpet player, you know. So that was very, very important to me, although I don't think the records turned out as well as Lionel would have liked them to, and I'm sure they weren't as good as the records he had already made with the more experienced musicians. Because Lionel had already made a lot of records with great musicians and including like I said King Cole and some of Benny Goodman's side men, and Teddy Wilson. And I can understand this.
